subject: Civil Engineering
title: Shotcrete: Sprayed Concrete Lining
description: A 60-second lesson on Shotcrete: Sprayed Concrete Lining.

hook.text: Seconds after blasting, wet concrete is sprayed onto raw rock — instant support.

buildup.text: Shotcrete is concrete projected at high velocity from a nozzle — it sticks to any surface.

discovery.text: Steel fibers mixed in replace traditional rebar — tougher, faster, and no formwork needed.

twist.text: Accelerators make shotcrete set in minutes — critical when loose rock could fall at any moment.

climax.text: Layer by layer, shotcrete builds up to a structural lining — 300mm thick or more.

punchline.text: Spray concrete on rock and it becomes a wall in minutes. Speed is survival underground.

quiz.question: Why is shotcrete preferred for immediate tunnel support after excavation?
options: It's cheaper than all other lining methods
It can be sprayed rapidly onto any surface without formwork, setting in minutes
Shotcrete is stronger than precast concrete segments
